results.summary: This design is a transmit-only BPSK baseband modulator that generates a PRBS-7 data stream, maps bits to +/-1 symbols, and shapes them with a polyphase root-raised-cosine filter. The output is an 8-bit signed sample bus. The PRBS-7 generator uses a 127-bit period that is short enough to verify by eye in a waveform. The design is intended for communication applications.

TinyMind SoC is a processor-controlled inference accelerator that classifies eight binary feature inputs into three classes using a custom CPU, program ROM, and a clocked TinyMind core with confidence logic. Results are shown on a seven-segment display, with a decimal point indicating a close prediction, and a CPU run-enable input on uio[0]. The design is a compact header filter rather than a full packet processor, and the documentation does not report silicon results. The accelerator is notable for its small size and educational potential.

This design is a spiking neural network with neuromorphic characteristics, implemented in analog circuitry. It includes a perceptron-based classifier and an ADC for input conversion. The design is intended for biomedical applications, such as detecting specific patterns in physiological signals. The documentation does not specify external hardware or silicon test results.

This design is an audio processing circuit that uses an I2S interface for digital audio input and output. It includes a PWM output, a DAC, and a comparator for analog signal processing. The design is intended for communication or audio applications. The documentation does not specify external hardware or silicon test results.

This project is an 8-bit modified RISC-V-inspired processor with four registers, four instructions in instruction memory, and one data-memory register, using a single 8-bit instruction encoding. It includes an ALU, a register file, and an SPI interface for external communication. The design is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating a simple processor architecture. The documentation does not report silicon results.

This design detects the tempo (BPM) of a live audio stream entirely in hardware, using onset detection and a bit-serial divider - no CPU, no multiplier. The documentation describes the algorithm in detail but does not report a testbench or silicon results, and no external hardware is specified. The design is notable for its purely hardware-based approach to audio analysis. It is intended for music or instrumentation applications.

It uses an SPI interface for data transfer and includes a DMA controller for efficient memory access. The design is intended for machine learning inference tasks. The documentation does not report silicon results.
